roads.label: Too little protein: one copy is lost
roads.description: One of the two gene copies no longer makes working protein, and the remaining copy is not enough (haploinsufficiency).

roads.label: Protein missing: both copies are lost
roads.description: Both gene copies are affected, so little or no working protein is made (recessive loss of function).

roads.label: Too little protein: unusual inheritance
roads.description: Loss of function with an inheritance pattern that is neither simple monoallelic nor biallelic (for example mitochondrial).

roads.label: Protein is overactive or does something new
roads.description: The altered protein works too much or in a new way (gain of function). Treatments that raise protein output would point the wrong way.

roads.label: A faulty protein interferes with the normal one
roads.description: The altered protein is made, and it disrupts the working protein from the other copy (dominant negative).

roads.label: Not a simple loss; exact mechanism unsettled
roads.description: Curators are confident the mechanism is not simple loss of function, but have not settled which other mechanism applies.

roads.label: Mechanism not established
roads.description: The curated source does not yet state how variants in this gene cause this condition.
